correctness.rationale: PASS: The logit transform is exactly canonical in physical time: p-dot=F(sigma(q)), q-dot=-G(sigma(p)), conserved H=V(p)+W(q) with V(0)=W(0)=0. Under increasing quadratic cross-payoffs with opposing endpoint signs, V,W are proper strictly convex potentials, so each noncentral level is one periodic oval. Direct antiderivative of G(sigma(p)) gives both slopes and beta intercepts and widths U_V(s)=As-B+o(1), U_W(s)=Cs-D+o(1). Coarea period T(E) is the convolution of branch-width derivatives, with positive decreasing integrable inverse-slope defects; the defect convolution vanishes while its one-body integrals cancel the potential minima, yielding T(E)=AC E-BC-AD+o(1). Four branch-arc travel times E/(a_i b_j)+O(1) and bounded time spent in compact logit strips give weak (not TV) independent Bernoulli corner law. The checker source symbolically differentiates potentials and runs bounded high-E trajectories, not a substitute for these all-E estimates.
residual_risks: High-energy numeric sample is not the analytic convergence proof.
